1170.title: Late medieval baseline
1170.text: The published reconstruction places most Jews in Asia and Africa, with much smaller populations in Western and Eastern Europe.

1300.title: European share rises
1300.text: Western Europe has become a much larger component of world Jewry, while the historical evidence remains fragmentary.

1490.title: On the eve of the Iberian expulsions
1490.text: This snapshot precedes the expulsions from Spain and Portugal and the subsequent redistribution toward the Mediterranean, Western Europe and elsewhere.

1700.title: Eastern Europe becomes central
1700.text: The balance within Europe has shifted sharply eastward; the Americas are still demographically tiny.

1825.title: Eastern European expansion
1825.text: Eastern Europe and the Balkans now contain roughly two-thirds of world Jewry in this reconstruction.

1880.title: Before mass transatlantic migration
1880.text: Eastern Europe is the overwhelming demographic center just as large-scale migration toward the Americas is accelerating.

1939.title: Prewar peak
1939.text: World Jewry is estimated at about 16.5 million. Europe still contains the majority, with a very large population already established in the Americas.

1948.title: After the Shoah; Israel is established
1948.text: The global population has fallen to about 11.5 million. The geographic balance is profoundly altered by the destruction of European Jewry and postwar migration.

1995.title: Two dominant poles emerge
1995.text: The Americas/Oceania and Asia/Africa buckets dominate the older classification; the latter contains Israel, whose share has risen dramatically.

2024.title: Israel and North America dominate
2024.text: Israel is 45.5% of world Jewry and the US alone is 40.0%; together Israel and the US account for more than 85% of the global core Jewish population.
